docs.title: Crackz
docs.text: AI-powered crack detection and analysis for harbor and bridge infrastructure.

docs.title: Welcome
docs.text:
Crackz is a commercial-grade crack detection solution designed for infrastructure inspection. Reduce inspection costs by up to 70% while improving safety and consistency through automated AI-powered analysis.

New to Crackz? Start with the Getting Started Guide to be up and running in minutes.

Ready to install? Check out the Installation Guide for setup instructions.

docs.title: For Infrastructure Managers
docs.text:
• Reduce costs – Process thousands of images in hours instead of weeks
  • Improve safety – Minimize physical inspections in hazardous locations
  • Early detection – Identify structural issues before they become critical
  • Proven ROI – Typical savings of $25,000-$75,000 annually per inspection program

docs.title: For Technical Teams
docs.text:
• Reproducible projects – Self-contained folder structure for complete traceability
  • Fast experimentation – Runtime overrides for rapid iteration
  • Scriptable & visual – Powerful CLI plus modern GUI
  • Container friendly – Docker images for all deployment scenarios
  • Extensible design – Modular AI pipeline built on PyTorch Lightning

docs.title: Model Capabilities
docs.text:
Crackz uses deep learning segmentation models to identify cracks at the pixel level:

  • Binary segmentation: Detect crack/no-crack with precise pixel masks
  • Multi-class segmentation: Identify multiple defect types (cracks, corrosion, spalling)
  • Flexible encoders: Choose from 20+ backbones (ResNet, EfficientNet, MobileNet, etc.)
  • Transfer learning: Leverage pre-trained ImageNet weights for better accuracy

docs.title: Two Deployment Paths
docs.text:
1. Use Pre-Trained Models (Fastest) - Quick deployment with ready-made checkpoints - Standard crack detection scenarios - Consistent results across sites

2. Train Custom Models (Most Accurate) - Domain-specific imagery and unique defect types - Maximum accuracy for your infrastructure - Requires labeled training data (images + masks)

See the Getting Started Guide for detailed workflows.

docs.title: Core Features
docs.text: Category Capabilities Interfaces CLI (crackz), GUI (crackz-gui), and Web Dashboard (Streamlit) Data Management Structured splits (raw/train/val/test) with automatic organization AI Pipeline Segmentation models with configurable encoders and metrics Logging Hybrid central + project logs for complete audit trails Configuration Pydantic-validated YAML configs with schema versioning Deployment Local, Docker (CPU/GPU), Azure Batch, standalone executables Training Runtime overrides for rapid experimentation

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text:
Every Crackz project is self-contained with complete traceability:

my-project/
├── images/           # Source images by split (raw/train/val/test)
├── masks/            # Ground truth for training
├── artifacts/        # Detection results and training metrics
├── logs/             # Complete audit trail
└── project.yaml      # Configuration snapshot

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
# Create project
crackz init --name demo

# Import images
crackz import-images --project demo --src ./photos --type raw --size 512 512

# Run detection
crackz detect run --project demo

# View results in demo/artifacts/detections/

Or use the GUI: 

crackz-gui
# File → New Project → Import Images → Run Detection

docs.title: Project Scope
docs.text: What we're building and why

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Crackz is a commercial AI-powered image analysis tool for detecting cracks in harbor and bridge infrastructure. It provides maritime engineers and infrastructure inspectors with automated crack detection to improve safety assessments and reduce manual inspection time.

docs.title: Primary Objectives
docs.text:
1. Automate crack detection in harbor concrete structures
  2. Reduce inspection time from manual visual inspection to automated analysis
  3. Improve detection accuracy with AI-powered segmentation models
  4. Enable enterprise deployment with Docker, GPU support, and team management
  5. Support offline operation for maritime environments with limited connectivity

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• Detection accuracy >85% IoU on validation sets
  • Processing speed <5 seconds per image on CPU
  • Memory usage <4GB RAM for standard workflows
  • Successful deployment to 5+ customer organizations
  • 95% customer satisfaction with detection quality

docs.title: Primary Users
docs.text:
1. Harbor Inspection Engineers
  2. Need: Fast, reliable crack detection for routine inspections
  3. Pain point: Manual inspection is time-consuming and subjective

  4. Success: Reduce inspection time by 60%

  5. Infrastructure Managers

  6. Need: Historical tracking of crack progression over time
  7. Pain point: Inconsistent documentation across inspections

  8. Success: Reproducible project structure with versioned results

  9. Maritime Authorities

  10. Need: Compliance reporting with standardized detection metrics
  11. Pain point: Manual report generation from inspection photos
  12. Success: Automated reporting with PDF export and GPS mapping

docs.text:

  2. Data Scientists (model training and tuning)
  3. Bridge Inspectors (similar use case to harbors)

docs.title: Technical Constraints
docs.text:
1. Python 3.11+ minimum (3.13 recommended for performance)
  2. PyTorch ecosystem (switching ML frameworks not feasible)
  3. YAML-based config for human readability (no binary configs)
  4. Backward compatibility for project schemas (must support migration)
  5. Offline-first design (no required internet connectivity)

docs.title: Performance Constraints
docs.text:
1. Memory: Must run on laptops with 8GB RAM (4GB allocated)
  2. CPU speed: <5 seconds per image on modern Intel/AMD CPUs
  3. GPU training: Support CUDA 11.8+ and 12.x
  4. Container startup: <30 seconds cold start
  5. Test coverage: Minimum 75% (enforced in CI)

docs.title: Business Constraints
docs.text:
1. Commercial licensing: GPL-3.0 source-available model
  2. Enterprise deployment: Must support air-gapped environments
  3. Customer support: Email support within 24 hours
  4. Data privacy: No telemetry, no cloud-required features
  5. Stability: No breaking changes without major version bump

docs.title: Development Constraints
docs.text:
1. CI/CD: All tests must pass on GitHub Actions
  2. Code quality: Ruff linting, mypy type checking enforced
  3. Documentation: All public APIs must be documented
  4. Performance: No regressions >20% without justification
  5. Git workflow: No direct pushes to main, all changes via PR

docs.title: Explicitly Out of Scope
docs.text:
1. Real-time video detection (focus on still images)
  2. 3D reconstruction (2D segmentation only)
  3. Mobile-first UI (desktop and CLI focus)
  4. Multi-user collaboration (single-user project management)
  5. Cloud storage integration (local storage only)
  6. Third-party API dependencies (self-contained operation)

docs.title: Why These Are Out of Scope
docs.text:
• Real-time video: Harbor inspections use high-res still photos, not video
  • 3D reconstruction: Not required by customers, adds complexity
  • Mobile-first: Harbor engineers use laptops/tablets with keyboards
  • Multi-user collaboration: Single inspector per project is current workflow
  • Cloud storage: Customer data privacy requirements favor local storage
  • Third-party APIs: Offline operation is critical for maritime environments

docs.title: Graphify for Agents
docs.text: This document explains how agents (Claude, other AI models) can use the Crackz knowledge graph to understand architecture and make better decisions.

docs.title: 1. Query the Graph Directly
docs.text:
# Agent: "Understand what ModelRegistry does"
graphify explain "ModelRegistry"

# Agent: "How does training work?"
graphify query "trace the training pipeline"

# Agent: "Should mask editing be in GUI or CLI?"
graphify path "masks_cli" "MaskEditorDialog"

docs.title: 2. Use Query Shortcuts
docs.text:
# Run common queries without MCP
./scripts/graphify-queries.sh god-nodes
./scripts/graphify-queries.sh architecture
./scripts/graphify-queries.sh cli-gui-boundary
./scripts/graphify-queries.sh training-pipeline
./scripts/graphify-queries.sh surprising

# See all available queries
./scripts/graphify-queries.sh list

docs.title: 3. MCP Server (Structured Tool Calls)
docs.text:
Start the server: 

./scripts/mcp-server.sh start

Agents can then call these tools programmatically:

Tool: query_graph
Input: "What does the Project class do?"
Output: [subgraph with explanation]

Tool: get_node
Input: "ModelRegistry"
Output: {id, label, connections, file location}

Tool: shortest_path
Input: {source: "MainWindow", target: "AIChatService"}
Output: [edge chain showing path]

Tool: god_nodes
Output: [top 10 highest-connectivity nodes]

Tool: get_community
Input: 0
Output: [all 54 nodes in community 0]

docs.title: God Nodes (Most Connected Abstractions)
docs.text:
ModelRegistry (79 edges) - Controls all model lifecycle (creation, loading, checkpointing) - Central bottleneck—all model work flows through here - Agent tip: Before adding model features, check if ModelRegistry should handle it

QtAppState (63 edges) - GUI state management - Used by all views for reactive updates - Agent tip: For GUI features, mutations go through QtAppState

MainWindow (62 edges) - Top-level container, orchestrates all panels - Agent tip: New tabs/panels registered here

AIChatService (57 edges) - LLM integration (chat, embedding, inference) - Agent tip: For AI features, implement here or call AIChatService

Project (46 edges) ⚠️ Chokepoint - Configuration hub—spans 23 communities - Agent tip: High coupling risk—consider splitting

docs.title: Surprising Connections (Refactoring Targets)
docs.text:
CLI→GUI Violation - masks_cli.py imports MaskEditorDialog from GUI - Violates layer separation (CLI shouldn't know about GUI) - Agent recommendation: Abstract through a service layer

Test→Core Tight Coupling - Tests import internal functions, not just public APIs - Makes refactoring risky - Agent recommendation: Enforce test→public API only

Project Spans 23 Communities - Indicates over-responsibilities - Agent recommendation: Split into ProjectConfig, ProjectMetadata, ProjectImport

docs.title: Communities (Tight Coupling Zones)
docs.text:
Community Purpose Nodes Cohesion 0 Annotation config 54 0.04 1 Database layer 33 0.04 2 Training pipeline 25 0.04 ... ... ... ...

Agent tip: Code in the same community is tightly coupled. Avoid creating dependencies between communities.

docs.title: Using Graph Data in Code Decisions
Example 1: Where Should New Feature Go?
docs.text:
Agent question: "I need to add a new model type. Where in the codebase?"

Graph exploration: 

graphify explain "ModelRegistry"
graphify query "what creates models?"
graphify path "MainWindow" "ModelRegistry"

Output: ModelRegistry is the central hub for all models. New types should register there.

docs.title: Example 2: Is This Coupling a Problem?
docs.text:
Agent question: "Should CLI call GUI? They're in different layers."

Graph exploration: 

graphify path "masks_cli" "MaskEditorDialog"
graphify query "what other CLI->GUI calls exist?"

Output: This is a known surprise connection—indicates missing abstraction layer.

docs.title: Example 3: Can I Refactor This?
docs.text:
Agent question: "Project is coupled to everything. Can I safely split it?"

Graph exploration: 

graphify explain "Project"
graphify query "what depends on Project?"
graphify get_community 38  # Project's community

Output: Project has 46 edges across 23 communities. Safe refactoring: extract ProjectConfig (used for initialization), ProjectMetadata (runtime info), ProjectImport (data loading).

docs.title: MCP Integration for Claude Desktop
docs.text:
If using Claude Desktop, add to ~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "graphify": {
      "command": "python3",
      "args": ["-m", "graphify.serve", "/absolute/path/to/graphify-out/graph.json"]
    }
  }
}

Then Claude can query the graph while coding: 

[Claude is now connected to Graphify tools]
Claude: "Before I add this feature, let me query the graph..."
[Claude automatically calls query_graph, shortest_path, etc.]

docs.title: Keeping Graph Current
docs.text:
Auto-update on commits: 

git commit -m "feat: add new model type"
# Post-commit hook runs automatically
# Graph updated with new code

Manual update after big refactor: 

./scripts/graphify-queries.sh surprising  # See new surprises
graphify . --update                        # Re-extract changed files
./scripts/mcp-server.sh restart            # Restart for agents

docs.title: "Understand the architecture"
docs.text:
./scripts/graphify-queries.sh all
Output: God nodes, main components, surprising connections

docs.title: "Where should this go?"
docs.text:
graphify explain "TargetModule"
graphify path "CurrentLocation" "TargetModule"
Output: Community membership, distance, dependencies

docs.title: "Is this coupled?"
docs.text:
graphify query "what connects X to Y?"
Output: All paths, edge confidence, source files

docs.title: "What's a good design pattern?"
docs.text:
graphify query "how do other modules do X?"
Output: Similar code patterns from other communities

docs.title: "Can I refactor this?"
docs.text:
graphify explain "ClassToRefactor"
graphify query "what depends on ClassToRefactor?"
Output: All dependents, refactoring risk assessment

docs.title: Performance Tips for Agents
docs.text:
1. Start with god nodes 

    graphify explain "ModelRegistry"  # Fast, high-value overview

  2. Use path queries for specific flows 

    graphify path "A" "B"  # Direct, focused answer

  3. Query before implementing

  4. Ask graph: "Does this pattern exist elsewhere?"

  5. Copy similar implementation, avoid inventing new patterns

  6. Check surprising connections before refactoring 

    ./scripts/graphify-queries.sh surprising

  7. Unexpected edges often indicate hidden requirements

  8. Use communities to scope changes 

    graphify get_community 0  # See all tight-coupled code

  9. Changes within a community have less cross-community impact

docs.title: Graphify Setup for Crackz
docs.text: This directory contains infrastructure for the Crackz automated knowledge graph—built from code structure analysis.

docs.title: 1. Knowledge Graph (graphify-out/)
docs.text:
• graph.json — the core graph (6,555 nodes, 10,806 edges)
  • GRAPH_REPORT.md — audit report with god nodes, surprises, suggested questions
  • obsidian/ — Obsidian vault export for local PKM + visualization

docs.title: 2. Post-Commit Hook (.git/hooks/post-commit)
docs.text: Auto-rebuilds the graph on every code commit. Detects changed code files and re-runs AST extraction (fast, free).

docs.title: 3. MkDocs Integration (docs/architecture/graph.md)
docs.text: Embedded in the developer documentation site. References the graph for architecture insight.

docs.title: Open the Graph
docs.text:
Option A: Obsidian (Recommended for exploration) 

open graphify-out/obsidian
# Then: Open as Vault in Obsidian.app
# Features: Graph view, canvas, full-text search, backlinks

Option B: GraphML (Gephi, yEd) 

# Export if needed:
graphify graphify-out --graphml
open graphify-out/graph.graphml

docs.title: Query from CLI
docs.text:
# What does ModelRegistry do?
graphify explain "ModelRegistry"

# Find shortest path
graphify path "MainWindow" "AIChatService"

# Find connections to a concept
graphify query "what imports do Project and Train share?"

docs.title: View in Docs
docs.text: Open http://localhost:8000/architecture/graph.html (after mkdocs serve)

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. AST Extraction (runs on commit)
  2. Parses Python/TypeScript/Go/etc code
  3. Extracts: imports, calls, class hierarchies, type annotations

  4. Results: graph.json (fully deterministic, no LLM needed)

  5. Clustering (runs on commit)

  6. Detects communities (tightly connected code regions)
  7. Scores cohesion per community

  8. Results: community assignments in graph.json

  9. Analysis (runs on commit)

  10. Finds god nodes (highest connectivity)
  11. Finds surprising connections (cross-community edges)

  12. Suggests architectural questions

  13. Visualization

  14. Obsidian canvas + graph view
  15. HTML (too large for browser, use Obsidian or Gephi)
  16. GraphML (for Gephi, yEd)

docs.title: Rebuild on Demand
docs.text:
# Full rebuild (all code files)
graphify .

# Incremental update (only changed files)
graphify . --update

# Re-cluster only (if you changed community labels)
graphify . --cluster-only

docs.title: Post-Commit Hook Control
docs.text:
# Disable
rm .git/hooks/pre-push

# Re-enable
# Hook will be reinstalled on next setup

# Manual rebuild after big refactor
graphify . --update

docs.title: Semantic Enrichment (requires LLM)
docs.text:
The current setup uses AST-only mode (free, no API calls). To add semantic analysis (cross-file patterns, design rationale):

# With Claude API
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-... graphify . --mode deep

# With local Ollama (experimental)
OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434 graphify . --mode deep

This adds confidence about inferred relationships and design insights, but costs tokens.

docs.title: Key Insights
docs.text:
God Nodes (architectural chokepoints): - ModelRegistry (79 edges) — all models flow through here - QtAppState (63 edges) — GUI state center - Project (46 edges) — configuration hub, spans 23 communities - MainWindow (62 edges) — top-level container - train() (various edges) — training orchestration

Surprising Connections (refactoring opportunities): - CLI layer (_do_edit_mask) calls GUI layer (MaskEditorDialog) - Tests reach deep into core config, not just public APIs - Training reaches into metrics cleanup

Risk Areas: - Project is highly coupled (spans 23 communities) - Test-core coupling is tight (tests call internal functions) - CLI-GUI boundary is blurry (both direction calls)

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Graph is empty 

# Check if code files were detected
graphify . --no-semantic  # Dry run
# Check graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md for errors

Post-commit hook not running 

# Ensure it's executable
chmod +x .git/hooks/post-commit

# Test manually
.git/hooks/post-commit

# Check git config
git config --get-all hooks.postcommit

Obsidian vault is huge (6500 notes) - Don't worry, this is normal for a large codebase - Use search + backlinks instead of browsing - Enable graph clustering visualization (Obsidian.app → Graph view → settings)

Want to exclude certain directories Edit .graphifyignore in repo root (same format as .gitignore), then rebuild: 

graphify . --update

docs.title: Advanced Performance & Reproducibility
docs.text: This page describes optional settings for faster training / inference and more reproducible runs.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Advanced knobs live under ai.training and ai.detection in the project YAML (or unified ProjectConfig). They are all optional and default to safe, CPU‑friendly values.

Area Field Location Purpose Precision precision ai.training Mixed precision / bfloat16 acceleration Devices devices ai.training Number of devices (GPUs) for distributed training Strategy strategy ai.training PyTorch Lightning strategy (e.g. ddp) Reproducibility seed ai.training, ai.detection Sets global RNGs (python/numpy/torch/lightning)

docs.title: Mixed Precision
docs.text:
Mixed precision can significantly improve throughput on modern GPUs.

Supported values (Lightning compatible): - 16 or 16-mixed – FP16 mixed precision - bf16-mixed – bfloat16 mixed precision (Ampere + some CPUs) - 32 – (default if omitted)

Example: 

ai:
  training:
    precision: 16-mixed
    batch_size: 16
CLI run: 
crackz detect train --project demo-project
(Precision is read from project YAML; no extra flag required.)

docs.title: Multi-GPU / Distributed Training
docs.text:
Enable multi-GPU training by specifying devices > 1 and a suitable strategy (usually ddp).

ai:
  training:
    devices: 2
    strategy: ddp
    batch_size: 8
    precision: bf16-mixed

Run (assuming 2 visible GPUs): 

crackz detect train --project demo-project

Docker (GPU): 

docker run --gpus all --rm -v %cd%\project:/home/app crackz-cli:gpu \
  detect train --project /home/app/demo-project

docs.title: Strategies Cheat Sheet
docs.text: Strategy Use Case Notes ddp Standard multi-GPU Best default on Linux ddp_spawn Windows / Jupyter Slight overhead auto Let Lightning decide Conservative choice

docs.title: Seeding & Reproducibility
docs.text:
Set seed in either training or detection sections: 

ai:
  training:
    seed: 1234
  detection:
    seed: 1234
Effect: - Sets PYTHONHASHSEED, python random, numpy, torch (CPU + CUDA), and Lightning worker seeds. - Does NOT force deterministic convolution algorithms (can slow performance). Add those manually if needed: 
import torch
torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• GPU kernels may still introduce nondeterminism (atomic ops, etc.).
  • Different hardware / driver stacks can still change results slightly.

docs.title: Example Comprehensive YAML
docs.text:
project:
  name: demo-project
  description: Perf tuned
paths:
  project_path: demo-project
  image_path: demo-project/images
  image_mask_path: demo-project/masks
  artifacts_path: demo-project/artifacts
logging:
  level: INFO
  log_dir: logs
ai:
  model:
    encoder: resnet34
    device: cuda
    input_size: [512, 512]
    threshold: 0.5
  training:
    batch_size: 16
    epochs: 20
    learning_rate: 0.0005
    precision: 16-mixed
    devices: 2
    strategy: ddp
    seed: 4242
  detection:
    batch_size: 8
    seed: 4242

docs.title: Workflow Tips
docs.text: Goal Tip Prototype quickly Keep CPU defaults; small batch, epochs=1, precision unset Throughput Increase batch_size gradually; enable 16-mixed precision Large model memory Use bf16-mixed (if supported) or reduce batch_size Reproducible baseline Fix seed; export config (crackz export-config)

docs.title: Exporting a Tuned Config
docs.text:
After modifying fields inside the project YAML: 

crackz export-config --project demo-project --out tuned_config.yaml
Share tuned_config.yaml for reproducible runs.

docs.title: Detection Phase Seeds
docs.text: Providing ai.detection.seed ensures preprocessing ordering / transforms (if later added) are deterministic between runs.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Issue Suggestion OOM errors Lower batch_size or remove mixed precision Slower than expected Ensure CUDA visible; confirm precision active in logs DDP hang Use ddp_spawn on Windows or for notebook contexts Seed ineffective Check for non-deterministic ops; set torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)

docs.text:

  • See CLI Cookbook for usage patterns
  • Open an issue for additional tuner hooks (gradient accumulation, profiling)

docs.title: Agent Playbook
docs.text: Shared repo-level guidance for Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Claude Code in Crackz.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Keep project guidance in the repository and keep user-level configuration personal. Use this file as the source of truth for project-specific agent behavior.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Read in this order unless the task is extremely narrow:

  1. CONTEXT.md
  2. PLAYBOOK.md
  3. This file
  4. Relevant focused docs:
  5. docs/architecture-guidelines.md
  6. docs/03-tasks.md
  7. PRODUCT_ROADMAP.md

docs.title: Project Standards
docs.text:
• Use Python 3.13 conventions already present in the repo.
  • Use uv for package management and execution. Do not use pip or conda.
  • Use uv run task ... for standard workflows where a task exists.
  • Use typer.secho() for end-user CLI output and logger from crackz.log for technical output.
  • Reuse centralized CLI options from core/src/crackz/cli/options.py.
  • Use pathlib.Path and keep code/tests platform-agnostic.
  • Prefer minimal, focused changes over broad refactors.
  • Add or update tests when behavior changes.
  • Lazy imports in the GUI: heavy libraries (PIL, numpy, diskcache, torch) must be imported inside the function or method that first needs them, never at module level in GUI entry-point modules (app.py, app_state.py, views, panels). This keeps startup fast. Use TYPE_CHECKING blocks for type annotations that reference these types.

docs.title: Git Workflow Default
docs.text:
• Default to working on a branch and opening a pull request.
  • Do not commit directly to main unless the user explicitly instructs you to do so.
  • When addressing PR feedback or follow-up fixes, continue working on the same branch associated with that PR unless the user explicitly asks to use a different branch.
  • Treat direct pushes to main as an exception that requires explicit user instruction.

docs.title: Worktrees
docs.text:
• Prefer a separate git worktree when it helps keep unrelated local changes untouched.
  • Use a worktree for parallel branch work, PR follow-up fixes, or review tasks that should not disturb the current working tree.
  • Do not create a worktree by default; use one when it clearly reduces risk, context switching, or branch confusion.
  • If using a worktree, keep ownership clear: one branch per worktree, and do not mix unrelated tasks in the same worktree.

docs.title: Protected Files
docs.text:
Treat these as protected unless the task explicitly requires changing them:

  • .env
  • uv.lock
  • .pre-commit-config*

docs.title: Validation Ladder
docs.text:
Run the smallest relevant checks first.

  1. Targeted lint/format for touched Python files:
  2. uv run ruff check --fix <path>
  3. uv run ruff format <path>
  4. Targeted type check when signatures or public APIs changed:
  5. uv run mypy <path>
  6. Targeted tests for changed behavior:
  7. uv run pytest <test>
  8. Broader tasks only when warranted:
  9. uv run task tests
  10. uv run task integration
  11. uv run task build_docs

docs.title: Push Readiness
docs.text:
• Before pushing, run the smallest relevant validation for the change using the Validation Ladder.
  • This typically includes targeted Ruff checks and formatting, targeted mypy when signatures or public APIs changed, and the appropriate unit tests for affected behavior.
  • Do not push changes that have not been validated at an appropriate scope unless the user explicitly instructs you to do so.

docs.title: Role Map
docs.text:
Use the Crackz-specific repo skills in .agents/skills when the task clearly matches:

  • crackz: default entry skill for general Crackz repository work
  • crackz-developer: general implementation, bug fixes, and small refactors
  • crackz-reviewer: focused review for bugs, regressions, and missing tests
  • crackz-docs-writer: docs and docstring work
  • crackz-docker-specialist: Dockerfiles, image variants, registry/CI container work
  • crackz-pytorch-expert: training, inference, metrics, and model pipeline work

docs.title: Repo Vs User Level
docs.text:
Keep these in the repository:

  • Project conventions and coding rules
  • Crackz-specific workflows
  • Role-specific skills tied to this codebase
  • Shared references and architecture context

Keep these at user level:

  • Personal trust settings
  • Local permissions and command allowlists
  • Personal plugins/connectors
  • Generic cross-repo skills you want everywhere
  • Secrets, tokens, auth state, machine-specific paths

docs.title: Codex
docs.text:
• Reads AGENTS.md
  • Uses repo skills from .agents/skills
  • May also use personal skills from ~/.codex/skills

docs.title: GitHub Copilot
docs.text:
• Reads .github/copilot-instructions.md
  • Uses repo skills from .agents/skills
  • Uses personal skills from ~/.copilot/skills

docs.title: Claude Code
docs.text:
• Reads CLAUDE.md
  • Uses Claude-specific repo config in .claude/
  • May also use user settings in ~/.claude/

Claude supports extra repo-local hooks and agent definitions. Those are useful, but they are not portable. For Codex and Copilot, prefer expressing the same behavior in repo docs and repo skills.

docs.title: Default Operating Style
docs.text:
• Read only the files needed for the task plus nearby interfaces.
  • Avoid full-repo scans unless the task actually requires them.
  • Do not change unrelated files.
  • Prefer direct execution over long planning for small tasks.
  • For larger tasks, make a short plan and then execute.
  • Summaries should be concise and include changed files, why they changed, and what was verified.

docs.title: AI Chat Assistant
docs.text:
The Crackz GUI includes an integrated AI chat assistant with multi-provider support. Choose between: - Anthropic (Direct): Direct API access to Claude models - OpenRouter: Unified gateway to 200+ models from 20+ providers

This feature provides real-time help with crack detection workflows, parameter tuning, and project management.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The AI chat assistant is a floating window that provides contextual help based on your current project state. It can:

  • Analyze your project configuration and suggest optimizations
  • Help tune detection parameters for better results
  • Explain crack detection concepts and workflows
  • Provide guidance on using Crackz features
  • Answer questions about your specific project

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
You need an API key from one of the following providers:

Option 1: Anthropic (Direct) - Get API key from Anthropic Console - Direct access to Claude models - Pricing: $3-15/MTok input, $15-75/MTok output

Option 2: OpenRouter (Recommended) - Get API key from OpenRouter - Access to 200+ models from 20+ providers - Cost savings: Up to 75% cheaper than direct (e.g., Claude Haiku: $0.25/MTok vs $1/MTok) - Additional models: GPT-4o, Llama 3.1, Gemini Pro, and more

Both require: - Internet connection for API communication

docs.title: Security Notice
docs.text:
API Key Storage

Your Anthropic API key is currently stored in plaintext in the application settings file.

For Development/Personal Use: - Keep the settings file secure with appropriate file permissions - Never commit the settings file to version control - Consider using environment variables for CI/CD

For Enterprise/Production Use: - Implement secure credential storage (Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain, etc.) - Use key rotation policies - Consider encrypted storage or external secret management systems - Review your organization's security policies before deployment

docs.title: Secure Storage with Keyring (Optional)
docs.text:
Crackz provides optional integration with the keyring library for secure credential storage. This uses your operating system's native secure storage:

  • Windows: Windows Credential Manager
  • macOS: Keychain
  • Linux: Secret Service (GNOME Keyring, KWallet, etc.)

Installation:

# Install keyring support
uv add keyring

# Or with pip
pip install keyring

Usage:

Once keyring is installed, you can use it programmatically in your Python scripts:

from crackz_gui.state.secure_storage import (
    store_api_key,
    retrieve_api_key,
    is_secure_storage_available,
)

# Check if keyring is available
if is_secure_storage_available():
    # Store API key securely
    store_api_key("your-api-key-here")

    # Retrieve API key
    api_key = retrieve_api_key()

    # Delete API key
    from crackz_gui.state.secure_storage import delete_api_key
    delete_api_key()
else:
    print("Keyring not available - falling back to plaintext storage")

Benefits:

  • ✅ Encrypted storage using OS-level encryption
  • ✅ No plaintext API keys in settings files
  • ✅ Cross-platform support (Windows/macOS/Linux)
  • ✅ Optional dependency - fallback to plaintext if not installed
  • ✅ Zero configuration - uses OS defaults automatically

Note: The GUI currently stores API keys in plaintext settings. Keyring integration is available for custom scripts and automation workflows. Full GUI integration is planned for a future release.

docs.title: Initial Setup
docs.text:
1. Open Chat Window:
  2. Press § (Swedish/Nordic keyboards)

  9. Enter API Key:
    • Paste your provider-specific API key
    • Format: sk-ant-... (Anthropic) or sk-or-... (OpenRouter)
  10. Select Model: Choose from provider-specific catalog
  11. Click Save

!!! tip "OpenRouter Recommended" OpenRouter provides up to 75% cost savings and access to 200+ models while maintaining Claude quality. Get a free API key at openrouter.ai/keys.

  1. Start Chatting:
  2. Type your question in the input box
  3. Press Enter to send
  4. Use Shift+Enter or Ctrl+Enter for multi-line messages

docs.title: Project Context
docs.text:
The AI assistant automatically has access to your current project context, including:

  • Project name and description
  • AI configuration (model, training parameters)
  • Detection settings (threshold, confidence, NMS)
  • Data splits (train/val/test image counts)
  • Training history and metrics

This allows the assistant to provide specific, actionable advice for your project.

docs.title: Tune Detection Parameters
docs.text:
You: My detection is finding too many false positives. How can I reduce them?

AI: Based on your project, I recommend:
1. Increase confidence_threshold from 0.25 to 0.4
2. Adjust iou_threshold to 0.5 for stricter overlap filtering
3. Consider retraining with more negative examples

Would you like me to explain how to adjust these in your project?

docs.title: Training Guidance
docs.text:
You: How many epochs should I train for?

AI: For your dataset with 150 training images:
- Start with 50 epochs as a baseline
- Monitor validation loss - it should decrease steadily
- If validation loss plateaus before 50 epochs, you can stop early
- If still improving at 50, try 75-100 epochs

Your current batch_size of 8 is good for this dataset size.

docs.title: Project Analysis
docs.text:
You: Analyze my project configuration

AI: Here's what I found in your oslo_project:
✅ Good splits: 70/20/10 train/val/test distribution
⚠️  Low image count (150 total) - consider data augmentation
✅ Reasonable batch_size (8) for dataset
💡 Suggestion: Enable data augmentation in training config
💡 Suggestion: Consider collecting more diverse training data

docs.title: Feature Questions
docs.text:
You: How do I export detection results to CSV?

AI: To export detection results:
1. Run detection: `crackz detect run <project>`
2. Results are saved in project/artifacts/detections/
3. Use export command: `crackz export --format csv <project>`

Or in GUI:
1. Click "Run Detection" button
2. Results appear in Detection Results panel
3. Click "Export" → "CSV Format"

docs.title: Character Limits
docs.text:
The input box has a character limit to ensure efficient API usage:

  • Up to 3,500 characters: Green indicator (optimal)
  • 3,500-3,800 characters: Orange indicator (warning)
  • Over 3,800 characters: Red indicator (too long)

If your message is too long, consider: - Breaking it into multiple smaller questions - Removing unnecessary details - Being more concise in your description

docs.title: API Key Storage
docs.text:
• API keys are stored locally in your application settings
  • Keys are never transmitted except to Anthropic's API
  • Consider using environment variables for production

docs.title: Data Sent to Claude
docs.text:
When you send a message, the following data is transmitted to Anthropic: - Your message text - Conversation history (previous messages in current session) - Project context (configuration, not images or training data)

Not sent: - Image files - Training data - Detection results (unless explicitly mentioned in your message)

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Don't include sensitive information in messages
  • Use project-specific terminology to get better help
  • Clear conversation history when switching projects

docs.title: "API key not configured"
docs.text: Solution: Click the ⚙ Settings button and enter your Anthropic API key.

docs.title: "Error code: 401 - invalid x-api-key"
docs.text: Solution: Your API key is invalid or expired. Get a new key from Anthropic Console.

docs.title: "Error code: 404 - model not found"
docs.text: Solution: The selected model doesn't exist. Open settings and select a valid model: - claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 - claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 - claude-opus-4-1-20250805

docs.title: Chat window won't open
docs.text: Solutions: - Try alternative keyboard shortcuts: §, ~, or Ctrl+/ - Use menu: Help → AI Chat Assistant - Check if window is behind main window (click taskbar icon)

docs.title: Slow responses
docs.text:
Causes: - Network latency - Model processing time (Opus is slower than Sonnet/Haiku) - Long conversation history

Solutions: - Clear conversation history (🗑️ Clear button) - Switch to Claude Haiku 4.5 for faster responses - Check your internet connection

docs.title: No project context in responses
docs.text: Solution: Make sure a project is loaded in the main GUI. The AI can only provide project-specific advice when a project is active.

To add more project context to the AI assistant:

  1. Edit ai_chat.py method _get_context(): 

    def _get_context(self) -> str:
    if self.app_state is None or self.app_state.project is None:
        return "No project loaded"

    project = self.app_state.project

    # Add your new context here
    return f"""
    Current project: {project.name}

    Your new context:
    - Additional info: {project.additional_info}
    """

  2. Context is automatically included in every message to Claude

from pathlib import Path
from crackz.project.project import load_project_from_path

docs.title: Create a New Project Programmatically

from pathlib import Path
from crackz.project.project import (
    ProjectMetadata, ProjectPaths, create_project, save_project
)

project = create_project(
    metadata=ProjectMetadata(name="demo-project", description="Example"),
    paths=ProjectPaths(
        project_path=Path("demo-project"),
        image_path=Path("demo-project/images"),
        image_mask_path=Path("demo-project/masks"),
        artifacts_path=Path("demo-project/artifacts"),
    ),
    force=False,
)
save_project(project)

docs.title: Settings (Environment / YAML)
docs.text:
CrackzSettings supports environment overrides with the prefix CRACKZ_ (e.g. CRACKZ_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG).

A module for managing and loading project configuration.

This module provides a configuration model and functionality to load the configuration from a YAML file.

Exceptions:

This module contains exception classes related to configuration errors.

The exceptions defined here are used to handle various errors that occur during the configuration or project lifecycle process, such as missing configuration files or invalid configuration content.

docs.title: CrackzSettings
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSettings

Configuration for a ai crackz project.

Source code in core/src/crackz/config/crackz_settings.py 
class CrackzSettings(BaseSettings):
    """Configuration for a ai crackz project."""

    name: str = "crackz_project"
    log_dir: Path = Path("logs")
    log_level: str = "INFO"

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(
        env_file=".env",
        env_prefix="CRACKZ_",
        case_sensitive=False,
    )

    @classmethod
    def from_conf(cls, conf_file: Path) -> "CrackzSettings":
        """
        Creates and returns an instance of the class from a configuration file.
        This method reads a YAML configuration file from the given file path, parses
        its content into a dictionary, and uses it to initialize and return an
        instance of the class.

        If the configuration file is empty, an empty dictionary will be used.
        If the file does not exist, FileNotFoundError is raised.
        :param conf_file: Path or str pointing to the YAML file.
        :return: A new instance of the class initialized with the configuration
                 data from the file.
        :rtype: CrackzSettings
        """
        if not conf_file.exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Configuration file not found: {conf_file!s}")

        try:
            with conf_file.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                data = yaml.safe_load(f) or {}
            return cls(**data)

        except FileNotFoundError as e:
            raise ConfigFileNotFoundError(f"Configuration file not found: {conf_file!s}") from e
        except yaml.YAMLError as e:
            raise InvalidConfigError(f"Error parsing YAML configuration {conf_file!s}: {e}") from e
        except Exception as e:
            raise ConfigError from e

docs.title: Unified Project Configuration (Scaffold)
docs.text:
A minimal serializable wrapper combining model/training/detection/logging settings.

Unified ProjectConfig scaffold.

This provides a light-weight configuration model that can be serialized independently of the full Project instance. It wraps the component models already defined in project.project and adds helper factory methods to construct a Project or persist the config.

Minimal by design - extend with additional global settings later (e.g. random seeds, mixed precision flags, registry URIs, feature toggles).

docs.title: ProjectConfig
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

Serializable project configuration wrapper (minimal).

Source code in core/src/crackz/config/project_config.py 
class ProjectConfig(BaseModel):
    """Serializable project configuration wrapper (minimal)."""

    name: str
    description: str = ""
    project_path: Path
    image_path: Path
    image_mask_path: Path
    artifacts_path: Path
    logging: LoggingConfig = LoggingConfig()
    model: ModelConfig = ModelConfig()
    training: TrainingConfig = TrainingConfig()
    detection: DetectionConfig = DetectionConfig()

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: Path) -> ProjectConfig:
        """Load the configuration from the given path."""
        data = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        return cls(**data)

    def save(self, path: Path) -> None:
        """Save the configuration to the given path."""
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            yaml.safe_dump(self.model_dump(mode="json"), f, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True)

    def to_project(self) -> Project:
        """Construct a ``Project`` from this ``ProjectConfig``."""
        return Project(
            project=ProjectMetadata(name=self.name, description=self.description),
            paths=ProjectPaths(
                project_path=self.project_path,
                image_path=self.image_path,
                image_mask_path=self.image_mask_path,
                artifacts_path=self.artifacts_path,
            ),
            logging=self.logging,
            ai=AIConfig(
                model=self.model,
                training=self.training,
                detection=self.detection,
            ),
        )

    @classmethod
    def from_project(cls, project: Project) -> ProjectConfig:
        """Construct a ``ProjectConfig`` from a ``Project``."""
        return cls(
            name=project.project.name,
            description=project.project.description,
            project_path=project.paths.project_path,
            image_path=project.paths.image_path,
            image_mask_path=project.paths.image_mask_path,
            artifacts_path=project.paths.artifacts_path,
            logging=project.logging,
            model=project.ai.model,
            training=project.ai.training,
            detection=project.ai.detection,
        )

docs.title: Project API
docs.text:
Project objects encapsulate paths, metadata, and convenience helpers.

A set of utility functions and classes to manage and manipulate project configurations.

This module provides functionality to create, configure, save, and manage project-related directories and metadata. It is optimized to handle common scenarios during project setup, including directory creation and YAML-based serialization for project configurations. All project configurations follow a fixed structure to ensure consistency during usage.

It includes: - A Pydantic-based Project model to define project metadata. - Functions to generate required project directories. - Functionality to serialize project configurations to persistent storage in YAML format.

Supporting types:

Project-level constants.

Exceptions:

This module defines custom exception classes related to project operations.

These exception classes inherit from CrackzError and represent specific errors encountered in the context of projects, such as configuration issues or file import errors.

docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

Represents a project model with configuration for storing project details.

The Project class encapsulates the essential attributes and configurations of a project. This includes details such as the project's name, description, creation date, and storage-related paths. Designed to work with a BaseModel-compatible configuration that ensures model extensibility. :

Source code in core/src/crackz/project/project.py 
class Project(BaseModel):
    """
    Represents a project model with configuration for storing project details.

    The Project class encapsulates the essential attributes and configurations of
    a project. This includes details such as the project's name, description,
    creation date, and storage-related paths. Designed to work with a
    BaseModel-compatible configuration that ensures model extensibility.
    :
    """

    project: ProjectMetadata
    paths: ProjectPaths
    logging: LoggingConfig
    ai: AIConfig
    annotation: AnnotationConfig = Field(default_factory=AnnotationConfig)
    data: DataConfig = DataConfig()  # Data preprocessing configuration
    schema_version: int | None = None  # Added for migration tracking

    model_config = {
        "ser_json_timedelta": "iso8601",
        "ser_json_bytes": "utf8",
    }

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _sync_annotation_derived_fields(self) -> Project:
        """Keep legacy model fields synchronized with the project annotation schema."""
        self.sync_derived_fields()
        return self

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        """The name of the project."""
        return self.project.name

    @property
    def root(self) -> Path:
        """Project root directory."""
        return Path(self.paths.project_path)

    @property
    def config_file(self) -> Path:
        """The expected config file name for this project."""
        return Path(f"{self.project.name}{PROJECT_FILE_SUFFIX}")

    @property
    def detections_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the detected images data directory.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the detected images data directory derived from the
                  provided image path.
        """
        return Path(self.paths.artifacts_path) / DETECTIONS_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def models_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the models directory (new structure).

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the models directory.
        """
        return Path(self.paths.artifacts_path) / MODELS_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def checkpoints_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the checkpoints directory.

        Deprecated: Use models_path instead. This property provides
        backward compatibility by checking for legacy 'checkpoints'
        directory and falling back to new 'models' directory.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the models directory (or legacy checkpoints for old projects).
        """
        warnings.warn(
            "checkpoints_path is deprecated and will be removed in a future version. "
            "Use models_path instead.",
            DeprecationWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )
        # For backward compatibility: if legacy checkpoints directory exists and models doesn't,
        # use the legacy directory. Otherwise use the new models directory.
        legacy_checkpoints_dir = Path(self.paths.artifacts_path) / CHECKPOINTS_DIR_NAME
        models_dir = self.models_path

        if legacy_checkpoints_dir.exists() and not models_dir.exists():
            return legacy_checkpoints_dir
        return models_dir

    @property
    def runtime_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the runtime directory for logs and temporary artifacts.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the runtime directory.
        """
        return self.paths.artifacts_path / RUNTIME_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def training_path(self) -> Path:
        """Gets the path to the training directory."""
        return self.paths.artifacts_path / TRAINING_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def detections_visualizations_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the detection visualizations subdirectory.

        For backward compatibility: if the new visualizations subdirectory doesn't exist
        or is empty (no PNG files), fall back to the legacy detections directory.
        This handles projects that were schema-migrated but not file-migrated.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the detection visualizations directory
                (or legacy detections for old projects).
        """
        visualizations_dir = self.detections_path / VISUALIZATIONS_DIR_NAME
        detections_dir = self.detections_path

        # Check if visualizations subdirectory exists and contains PNG files
        # Use next() for performance: stops at first match instead of iterating all files
        if visualizations_dir.exists() and next(visualizations_dir.glob("*.png"), None) is not None:
            return visualizations_dir

        # Otherwise, fall back to legacy detections directory (for backward compatibility)
        # This handles schema-migrated projects where files weren't moved
        return detections_dir

    @property
    def detection_results_path(self) -> Path:
        """Gets the path to the training metrics JSON file."""
        return self.paths.artifacts_path / DETECTIONS_DIR_NAME / "detection_results.json"

    @property
    def training_metrics_path(self) -> Path:
        """Gets the path to the training metrics JSON file."""
        return self.paths.artifacts_path / TRAINING_DIR_NAME / "training_metrics.json"

    @property
    def tensorboard_logs_path(self) -> Path:
        """Gets the path to the TensorBoard logs directory (in runtime/)."""
        return self.runtime_path / "tensorboard"

    @property
    def registry_db_path(self) -> Path:
        """Path to the per-project SQLite database (models, detection runs, epochs).

        Canonical name is ``project.db``. Legacy artifact-level ``crackz.db`` files
        are moved into this path by the registry layer.
        """
        artifacts_path = Path(self.paths.artifacts_path)
        if not artifacts_path.is_absolute():
            artifacts_path = Path(self.paths.project_path) / artifacts_path
        return artifacts_path / "project.db"

    @property
    def lightning_logs_path(self) -> Path:
        """Gets the path to the PyTorch Lightning logs directory (in runtime/)."""
        return self.runtime_path / "lightning_logs"

    @property
    def val_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the model validation data directory.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the validation data directory derived from the
                  provided image path.
        """
        return Path(self.paths.image_path) / VAL_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def test_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the model test data directory.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the test data directory derived from the
                  provided image path.
        """
        return Path(self.paths.image_path) / TEST_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def train_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the model train data directory.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the train data directory derived from the
                  provided image path.
        """
        return Path(self.paths.image_path) / TRAIN_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def train_mask_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the model train mask data directory.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the train data directory derived from the
                  provided image mask path.
        """
        return Path(self.paths.image_mask_path) / TRAIN_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def val_mask_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the model validation mask data directory.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the validation data directory derived from the
                  provided image mask path.
        """
        return Path(self.paths.image_mask_path) / VAL_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def test_mask_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the model test mask data directory.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the test data directory derived from the
                  provided image mask path.
        """
        return Path(self.paths.image_mask_path) / TEST_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def raw_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the raw (detect) test data directory.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the raw data directory derived from the
                  provided image path.
        """
        return Path(self.paths.image_path) / RAW_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def raw_mask_path(self) -> Path:
        """
        Gets the path to the raw mask (detect) test data directory.

        Returns:
            Path: The path to the raw data directory derived from the
                  provided image path.
        """
        return Path(self.paths.image_mask_path) / RAW_DIR_NAME

    @property
    def project_file_path(self) -> Path:
        """Compute the path where the project YAML will be saved."""
        return Path(self.paths.project_path) / f"{self.project.name}{PROJECT_FILE_SUFFIX}"

    def resolve_task_mode(self) -> Literal["binary", "multiclass"]:
        """Return the active segmentation task mode.

        Honors ``ai.model.task_mode`` when set; otherwise auto-derives from the
        annotation schema. ``"binary"`` collapses all foreground categories
        into a single defect-vs-none class.
        """
        explicit = self.ai.model.task_mode
        if explicit is not None:
            return explicit
        return "binary" if self.annotation.num_categories == 1 else "multiclass"

    def sync_derived_fields(self) -> None:
        """Update compatibility fields that are derived from project-owned schema state."""
        if self.resolve_task_mode() == "binary":
            self.ai.model.num_classes = 1
        else:
            self.ai.model.num_classes = self.annotation.num_label_ids

    @property
    def _image_ops(self) -> ImageOperations:
        """Get ImageOperations instance with current project paths."""
        return ImageOperations(
            image_path=Path(self.paths.image_path),
            image_mask_path=Path(self.paths.image_mask_path),
            train_path=self.train_path,
            val_path=self.val_path,
            test_path=self.test_path,
            raw_path=self.raw_path,
            train_mask_path=self.train_mask_path,
            val_mask_path=self.val_mask_path,
            test_mask_path=self.test_mask_path,
            raw_mask_path=self.raw_mask_path,
            mask_threshold=self.data.mask_threshold,
            preserve_mask_values=self.resolve_task_mode() == "multiclass",
            annotation=self.annotation,
        )

    def map_type_to_dir(self, image_type: ImagesType) -> Path:
        """
        Maps a given image type to its corresponding directory path.

        This method takes an image type as input and resolves it to a corresponding
        directory path. It supports types such as `raw`, `train`, `test`, and `val`.
        If the given value does not map to a valid type, the function defaults to the
        `raw` directory path.

        :param image_type: The type of the image to map ("raw", "train", "test", or "val").
        :return: The `Path` object representing the directory mapped from the given
                 image type, or `None` if no mapping exists.
        """
        return self._image_ops.map_type_to_dir(image_type)

    def map_type_to_masks_dir(self, image_type: ImagesType) -> Path:
        """
        Maps a given image type to its corresponding directory path.

        This method takes an image type as input and resolves it to a corresponding
        directory path. It supports types such as `raw`, `train`, `test`, and `val`.
        If the given value does not map to a valid type, the function defaults to the
        `raw` directory path.

        :param image_type: The type of the image mask to map ("raw", "train", "test", or "val").
        :return: The `Path` object representing the directory mapped from the given
                 image type, or `None` if no mapping exists.
        """
        return self._image_ops.map_type_to_masks_dir(image_type)

    def save_project(self) -> None:
        """
        Saves the given project to a file in YAML format. The function serializes
        the project data using the model's `model_dump` method, and writes it to
        a specified path. The path is determined dynamically based on the project
        information. Logging is performed to confirm success or log any errors
        encountered during the saving process.

        :param project: The project object to be saved. The project must implement
            the `model_dump` method for serialization.
        :return: None
        """
        try:
            path = self.project_file_path
            self.sync_derived_fields()
            if self.schema_version is None:
                from crackz.project.migration import CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION

                self.schema_version = CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION

            # Update Crackz version on save to track last modification
            from crackz.version import get_version

            self.project.crackz_version = get_version()

            with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                yaml.safe_dump(self.model_dump(mode="json"), f, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True)
            logger.info("Project '{}' saved successfully to {}.", self.project.name, path)
        except (OSError, yaml.YAMLError) as e:
            logger.exception("Error saving project '{}'", self.project.name or "<unknown>")
            raise ProjectError from e

    def import_image_files(
        self,
        files: list[Path],
        dest_dir: Path,
        size: SizeType | None = None,
        quality: int = 90,
        *,
        overwrite: bool = False,
        progress_cb: ProgressCallbackType = None,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Import specific image files into project storage.

        - Resizes and adjusts quality.
        - Writes to the given destination directory.
        - Raises ImageImportError on failure.
        """
        effective_size = size or (self.data.target_size, self.data.target_size)
        self.ai.model.input_size = effective_size
        self._image_ops.import_image_files(
            files=files,
            dest_dir=dest_dir,
            size=effective_size,
            quality=quality,
            overwrite=overwrite,
            progress_cb=progress_cb,

    def import_images(
        self,
        source_path: Path,
        masks_source_path: Path | None = None,
        image_type: ImagesType = ImagesType.RAW,
        size: SizeType | None = None,
        quality: int = 90,
        *,
        overwrite: bool = False,
        progress_cb: ProgressCallbackType = None,
        split: bool = False,
        train_ratio: float = 0.7,
        val_ratio: float = 0.15,
        test_ratio: float = 0.15,
        random_seed: int | None = None,
        mask_label_map: dict[int, int] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Import images (and optional masks) into project storage.

        - Resizes and adjusts quality.
        - Writes to type-specific image/mask destinations.
        - Skips masks if not provided or empty.
        - Raises ImageImportError on failure.
        - If split=True, automatically distributes images across train/val/test splits.
        """
        effective_size = size or (self.data.target_size, self.data.target_size)
        self.ai.model.input_size = effective_size
        self._image_ops.import_images(
            source_path=source_path,
            masks_source_path=masks_source_path,
            image_type=image_type,
            size=effective_size,
            quality=quality,
            overwrite=overwrite,
            progress_cb=progress_cb,

    def create_project_dir(self, *, force: bool) -> None:
        """
        Creates the necessary directories for a given project. If the directories already
        exist, it optionally allows overwriting them based on the `force` parameter.

        :param project: The project object containing the `project_path` and `artifacts_path `
        :param force: A boolean indicating whether to forcibly overwrite existing directories
        :return: None
        """
        create_dir(dir_name=self.paths.project_path, force=force)
        create_dir(dir_name=self.paths.artifacts_path, force=force)

        # Create new artifact subdirectories
        create_dir(dir_name=self.models_path, force=force)
        create_dir(dir_name=self.detections_path, force=force)
        # Always create visualizations subdirectory for new projects (don't use property here)
        create_dir(dir_name=self.detections_path / VISUALIZATIONS_DIR_NAME, force=force)
        create_dir(dir_name=self.training_path, force=force)
        create_dir(dir_name=self.runtime_path, force=force)

        setup_image_dir(image_path=Path(self.paths.image_path), force=force)
        setup_image_dir(image_path=Path(self.paths.image_mask_path), force=force)

    def _clean_models_selectively(self, models_path: Path) -> int:
        """Clean models directory while preserving best.ckpt.

        :param models_path: Path to models directory
        :return: Number of items removed
        """
        cleaned_count = 0
        if not models_path.exists():
            return cleaned_count

        # Remove checkpoint files except best.ckpt
        for ckpt_file in models_path.glob("*.ckpt"):
            if ckpt_file.name != "best.ckpt":
                ckpt_file.unlink(missing_ok=True)
                logger.info("Removed checkpoint: {}", ckpt_file)
                cleaned_count += 1

        # Remove non-checkpoint files (subdirectories are preserved)
        # This is intentional - subdirectories typically contain structured data
        # like TensorBoard logs that should be cleaned via their own paths
        for item in models_path.iterdir():
            if item.is_file() and item.suffix != ".ckpt":
                item.unlink(missing_ok=True)
                logger.info("Removed file: {}", item)
                cleaned_count += 1

        return cleaned_count

    def _remove_path(self, path: Path) -> int:
        """Remove a file or directory.

        :param path: Path to remove
        :return: 1 if removed, 0 otherwise
        """
        if not path.exists():
            return 0

        try:
            if path.is_dir():
                shutil.rmtree(path, ignore_errors=True)
                logger.info("Removed directory: {}", path)
            else:
                path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
                logger.info("Removed file: {}", path)
            return 1  # noqa: TRY300
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning("Failed to remove {}: {}", path, e)
            return 0

    def clean(self, *, logs_only: bool = False, keep_best_model: bool = True) -> int:
        """Clean temporary files and logs from the project.

        By default, cleans logs, training artifacts, models, and detections.
        Images and masks are always preserved. The best model checkpoint is preserved by default.

        :param logs_only: If True, only clean log files and runtime artifacts,
            preserve models/results
        :param keep_best_model: If True, preserve best.ckpt when cleaning models
        :return: Number of items removed
        """
        cleaned_count = 0

        # Always clean runtime directory and log files
        cleaned_count += self._remove_path(self.runtime_path)

        log_dir = Path(self.logging.log_dir)
        if log_dir.exists():
            for log_file in log_dir.glob("*.log"):
                cleaned_count += self._remove_path(log_file)

        if not logs_only:
            # Handle models directory
            if keep_best_model:
                cleaned_count += self._clean_models_selectively(self.models_path)
            else:
                cleaned_count += self._remove_path(self.models_path)

            # Clean detection results and training metrics
            cleaned_count += self._remove_path(self.detections_path)
            cleaned_count += self._remove_path(self.training_metrics_path)

        logger.info("Cleaned {} items from project '{}'", cleaned_count, self.name)
        return cleaned_count

def resolve_task_mode(self) -> Literal["binary", "multiclass"]:
    """Return the active segmentation task mode.

    Honors ``ai.model.task_mode`` when set; otherwise auto-derives from the
    annotation schema. ``"binary"`` collapses all foreground categories
    into a single defect-vs-none class.
    """
    explicit = self.ai.model.task_mode
    if explicit is not None:
        return explicit
    return "binary" if self.annotation.num_categories == 1 else "multiclass"

def clean(self, *, logs_only: bool = False, keep_best_model: bool = True) -> int:
    """Clean temporary files and logs from the project.

    By default, cleans logs, training artifacts, models, and detections.
    Images and masks are always preserved. The best model checkpoint is preserved by default.

    :param logs_only: If True, only clean log files and runtime artifacts,
        preserve models/results
    :param keep_best_model: If True, preserve best.ckpt when cleaning models
    :return: Number of items removed
    """
    cleaned_count = 0

    # Always clean runtime directory and log files
    cleaned_count += self._remove_path(self.runtime_path)

    log_dir = Path(self.logging.log_dir)
    if log_dir.exists():
        for log_file in log_dir.glob("*.log"):
            cleaned_count += self._remove_path(log_file)

    if not logs_only:
        # Handle models directory
        if keep_best_model:
            cleaned_count += self._clean_models_selectively(self.models_path)
        else:
            cleaned_count += self._remove_path(self.models_path)

        # Clean detection results and training metrics
        cleaned_count += self._remove_path(self.detections_path)
        cleaned_count += self._remove_path(self.training_metrics_path)

    logger.info("Cleaned {} items from project '{}'", cleaned_count, self.name)
    return cleaned_count

    :rtype: Project
    """
    # Create fresh copies to avoid shared mutable state issues with pytest-randomly
    if ai is None:
        ai = AIConfig(
            model=default_ai_config.model.model_copy(),
            training=default_ai_config.training.model_copy(),
            detection=default_ai_config.detection.model_copy(),
        )
    if logging is None:
        logging = default_logging_config.model_copy()

    # Set Crackz version on new projects
    if metadata.crackz_version is None:
        from crackz.version import get_version

        metadata.crackz_version = get_version()

    logger.info("Creating new project {}", metadata.name)
    project = Project(
        project=metadata,
        paths=paths,
        ai=ai,
        logging=logging,
    )
    project.create_project_dir(force=force)

    initialize_project_logging(project)

    return project

def load_project(project_file_path: Path) -> Project:
    """
    Loads a project configuration from the specified file path. The
    configuration file is expected to be in YAML format, and its content
    is deserialized into a `Project` object. If the file cannot be opened,
    read, or parsed, the function logs an error.

    Parameters:
        project_file_path (Path): The path to the project configuration file.

    Returns:
        Project | None: The deserialized `Project` object if loading is
        successful. Returns `None` if there is an error during the process.
    """
    try:
        project_file_path = Path(project_file_path)
        with project_file_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = yaml.safe_load(f) or {}
            project = Project(**data)
            if not Path(project.paths.project_path).is_absolute():
                project.paths.project_path = project_file_path.parent / project.paths.project_path
            logger.info(
                "Project '{}' loaded successfully to {}.",
                project.project.name,
                project_file_path,
            )
            initialize_project_logging(project)
            return project
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        logger.exception("Error loading project from '{}' - not found", project_file_path)
        raise ProjectNotFoundError from e
    except (OSError, yaml.YAMLError) as e:
        logger.exception("Error loading project from '{}'", project_file_path)
        raise ProjectConfigError from e
    except Exception as e:
        logger.exception("Error loading project from '{}'")
        raise ProjectError from e

def load_project_from_path(project_path: Path) -> Project:
    """
    Loads a project configuration from a specified path and returns a Project instance.

    This function reads a YAML file from the given project path, parses its content,
    and initializes a Project instance based on the data. If the file cannot be read
    or parsed, an appropriate exception is raised.

    :param project_path: The path to the project directory.
    :type project_path: Path
    :return: The initialized Project instance containing the configuration data.
    :rtype: Project
    :raises TypeError: Raised when there is an OSError or YAML parsing error while
        loading the project configuration.
    """
    try:
        project_name = project_path.stem
        project_file = project_path / f"{project_name}{PROJECT_FILE_SUFFIX}"
        with project_file.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = yaml.safe_load(f) or {}
            project = Project(**data)
            if not Path(project.paths.project_path).is_absolute():
                project.paths.project_path = project_path / project.paths.project_path
            logger.info(
                "Project '{}' loaded successfully to {}.", project.project.name, project_file
            )
            initialize_project_logging(project)
            return project
    except FileNotFoundError as e:
        logger.exception("Error loading project from '{}' - not found", project_path)
        raise ProjectNotFoundError from e
    except (OSError, yaml.YAMLError) as e:
        logger.exception("Error loading project from '{}'", project_path)
        raise ProjectConfigError from e

def load_from_project_path_or_cfg(cfg: Path | None, project_path: Path | None) -> Project:
    """
    Loads a project either from the provided project path or configuration file.

    This function attempts to load a project based on the provided parameters.
    If a project path is provided, the project is loaded from the given path.
    If a configuration file is provided instead, the project is loaded using
    the configuration file. The function prefers the project path if both are
    provided.

    :param cfg: Path to the configuration file for loading the project.
                Can be None if a project path is provided.
    :type cfg: Path | None
    :param project_path: Path to the project directory from which to load
                         the project. Can be None if a configuration file
                         is provided.
    :type project_path: Path | None
    :return: Returns the loaded project instance of type Project.
    :rtype: Project
    """
    if project_path is not None:
        return load_project_from_path(project_path)
    if cfg is not None:
        return load_project(cfg)
    msg = "Either cfg or project_path must be provided."
    logger.exception("Error loading project from '{}'", project_path)
    raise ProjectConfigError(msg)

docs.title: AI / Detection API
docs.text:
High‑level detection & training entry points:

AI detection compatibility exports with lazy loading.

This package intentionally avoids importing the full training/runtime stack at module import time so that lightweight paths such as report generation and CLI startup do not eagerly pull in PyTorch Lightning and segmentation models.

Datasets:

Dataset classes for crack images.

Dataloaders:

DataLoader utilities for crack images.

Model configuration & LightningModule wrapper:

The core CrackzModel class utilizes a segmentation backbone for binary or multiclass segmentation tasks. It computes segmentation logits, applies a task-aware combination loss (Dice + Focal for binary, Dice + CrossEntropy for multiclass) during training, and evaluates performance with IoU and accuracy metrics.

Per-task-mode behaviour (metric construction, loss selection, prediction shaping) lives in :mod:crackz.ai.model.segmentation.tasks — CrackzModel delegates to a :class:TaskStrategy rather than branching on task_mode at every call site.

Callbacks & utilities:

Custom callbacks for PyTorch Lightning.

This module provides callbacks for training and testing progress reporting, metrics collection, and image logging.

The ProgressCallback now includes batch-level progress tracking to provide more accurate time remaining estimates during training. Progress updates are reported every 10 batches (configurable) and at the end of each epoch, ensuring that the GUI and CLI show accurate remaining time even for long epochs with many batches.

Checkpoints:

Model checkpoint management utilities.

Visualization:

Visualization utilities for Crackz AI.

This package contains utilities for plotting, visualization, and graphical output of detection results and metrics.

Device management:

Device management and hardware utilities for Crackz AI.

This package contains utilities for device detection, hardware acceleration, and device-specific operations.

General utilities:

Utility package for Crackz AI - DEPRECATED.

This package has been broken up into more logical top-level packages: - crackz.ai.device: Device management and hardware utilities - crackz.ai.performance: Performance optimization and profiling utilities - crackz.ai.visualization: Plotting and visualization utilities - crackz.ai.pipeline: Workflow orchestration and cancellation support - crackz.ai.compat: Compatibility utilities for different environments - crackz.ai.core: Core types and protocols - crackz.ai.exceptions: AI-related exceptions

Please import directly from these packages instead of using crackz.ai.util.

Examples:

from crackz.ai.device import AIDevice, resolve_device_and_accelerator from crackz.ai.performance import RuntimeTracker, set_global_seed from crackz.ai.core import CrackzBatch, ProgressReporter

Exceptions:

Exceptions related to AI processing and pipeline errors.

This module defines custom exceptions for handling errors within the AI processing pipeline. It includes a hierarchy of exceptions that allow for more nuanced error handling in applications leveraging AI-related functionalities.

Classes:

Name Description AIPipelineError

Base class for AI-related exceptions.

ModelNotFoundError

Exception raised when a specified AI model cannot be found.

DataLoadingError

Exception raised when an error occurs during the data loading process.

def categorize_crack_severity(
    confidence: float,
    *,
    high_threshold: float = DEFAULT_HIGH_CONFIDENCE,
    medium_threshold: float = DEFAULT_MEDIUM_CONFIDENCE,
    has_crack: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """Categorize crack detection severity based on crack area percentage.

    This is the single source of truth for crack categorization across the application.
    Categories are simplified for user clarity: detected vs suspected cracks.

    Args:
        confidence: Crack area percentage as decimal (0.0 to 1.0)
                   Represents mean probability over whole image.
                   Typical values: 0.005-0.08 (0.5%-8% crack coverage)
        high_threshold: Threshold for "Crack Detected" category (default 0.05 = 5%)
        medium_threshold: Threshold for "Suspected Crack" category (default 0.02 = 2%)
        has_crack: Boolean flag indicating if crack was detected (confidence + area thresholds met)

    Returns:
        Severity category (one of three simplified categories):
            - "Crack Detected" (crack_area >= high_threshold OR has_crack=True)
            - "Suspected Crack" (medium_threshold <= crack_area < high_threshold)
            - "No Crack" (crack_area < medium_threshold)

    Examples:
        >>> categorize_crack_severity(0.08)  # 8% crack area
        'Crack Detected'
        >>> categorize_crack_severity(0.03)  # 3% crack area
        'Suspected Crack'
        >>> categorize_crack_severity(0.01)  # 1% crack area
        'No Crack'
        >>> categorize_crack_severity(0.01, has_crack=True)
        'Crack Detected'  # has_crack flag indicates both confidence and area thresholds met
    """
    # Prioritize has_crack flag (indicates confidence + area thresholds met)
    if has_crack or confidence >= high_threshold:
        return "Crack Detected"
    if confidence >= medium_threshold:
        return "Suspected Crack"
    return "No Crack"
